src: U.S. Census Bureau, cartographic boundary file cb_2020_us_cd116_500k
cd.vint: The Census Bureau's lines of the 116th Congress's districts (its file says session 116). The Bureau published no file of the 117th Congress's districts, the Congress the 2020 election chose.
rec: Revised Statutes of Missouri 128.346: the 2011 districts (ss. 128.451-128.458) are effective for the 113th through 117th Congress elections; the 2022 districts (ss. 128.461-128.468) for the 118th and 119th

Eight districts (the state lost a seat after the 2010 census). Both houses passed it in April 2011; the General Assembly overrode the Governor's veto on May 4, 2011. The Missouri Supreme Court upheld it (Pearson v. Koster, 2012). Effective for the 113th through 117th Congress elections, 2012 through 2020. Census check: cb_2020_us_cd116 (CDSESSN 116; lines supplied by the states by May 1, 2018) holds this plan; 8 of 8 districts differ in shape from the 2022 file, as a new plan should.

src: U.S. Census Bureau, cartographic boundary file cb_2020_us_sldu_500k
sldu.vint: The Census Bureau's 2020 file of legislative districts, the lines it records for the 2018 legislative session year. The Bureau published no file of the lines in use for 2020. Where a state's lines changed in between, the check below or the plan cited stops the map.
rec: 2012 Senate plan filed by the second Senate Apportionment Commission (after Teichman v. Carnahan): 34 districts

Missouri Office of Administration, Redistricting Commission Histories (June 23, 2021): 2011 House plan filed by the Appellate Apportionment Commission Nov. 30, 2011; 2011 Senate plan filed Mar. 12, 2012 after Teichman v. Carnahan (Jan. 17, 2012)

The first Senate plans (Appellate Apportionment Commission, filed Nov. 30 and Dec. 9, 2011) were thrown out by the Missouri Supreme Court on Jan. 17, 2012; the new commission filed this plan Mar. 12, 2012. Used for the 2012 through 2020 elections; half the Senate is elected every two years. Census check: cb_2020_us_sldu (LSY 2018, 34 districts; boundaries collected for the 2018 election year) holds this plan, which was unchanged to November 2020; 34 of 34 districts differ in shape from the 2022 file.

src: U.S. Census Bureau, cartographic boundary file cb_2020_us_sldl_500k
sldl.vint: The Census Bureau's 2020 file of legislative districts, the lines it records for the 2018 legislative session year. The Bureau published no file of the lines in use for 2020. Where a state's lines changed in between, the check below or the plan cited stops the map.
rec: 2011 House plan filed by the Appellate Apportionment Commission on Nov. 30, 2011: 163 districts

Missouri Office of Administration, Redistricting Commission Histories (June 23, 2021): 2011 House plan filed by the Appellate Apportionment Commission Nov. 30, 2011; 2011 Senate plan filed Mar. 12, 2012 after Teichman v. Carnahan (Jan. 17, 2012)

The House commission could not agree, so six appellate judges drew the plan; challenges to it were reported rejected by the Missouri Supreme Court in 2012. Used for the 2012 through 2020 elections. Census check: cb_2020_us_sldl (LSY 2018, 163 districts; boundaries collected for the 2018 election year) holds this plan, which was unchanged to November 2020; 160 of 163 districts differ in shape from the 2022 file.
